description.p: Azzurro is a controller for BluOS players — Bluesound, NAD and PSB. It finds the players on your network and talks to them directly, with no cloud service in between and no account of its own. Music services stay signed in on the player.
Each player describes its own browse screens, and Azzurro draws what it is given, so a music service that BluOS adds later can be browsed and played without an update to the app.

ul.li: Finds players by broadcast, and remembers ones that discovery cannot reach
Now playing with cover art, seeking, shuffle, repeat and a sleep timer
The play queue, with a context menu on every track
Browse and search every source the player offers, including music services
Group players together for multi-room playback
Each player appears separately in the desktop's own media controls, so the media keys work

description.p: Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Lenbrook Industries. BluOS, Bluesound, NAD, PSB and MQA are their trademarks.
Players that move, stop answering or come back are handled as they should be.

ul.li: A player that takes a new address while the app is closed is recognized and followed, instead of being left behind as a second row that never answers.
A player that has stopped responding can be forgotten from the player list, and the window no longer starts on one that does not answer.
Choosing a player that is not responding says so instead of showing another player's screens, and its screens appear once it answers again.
Grouping is offered only between players that can take part in it.
Every control has a name and a role for screen readers, keys go to the pane in front, and text being typed is kept.
The quality badge says what the player's decoder found, MQA included, and keeps it through a pause and across a restart.
Windows gets an installer with a Start Menu entry, and the Flatpak moves to the 26.08 runtime.
